body:
# Independent audit: all-dimensional affine-roof nongluing lift


`candidate 60dfb1dd651b7ddd`.
Result: **PASS** for every d>=3. The planar projection is genuinely
truncated by the roof; using the original untruncated quadrilaterals
as the projection would have been incorrect, but the source uses the
correct truncated sets in its nonhomothety argument.

## 1. Actual lifted bodies and their common interior point

Let m=d-2>=1. The lifted sets are intersections of the planar polygon
cylinders with the closed affine constraints

    t_j>=0,
    sum_j t_j<=phi_A(x,y)=19-11x-y,

and similarly with constants 14 and 33/2 for B and K. Thus they are
closed and convex. Their planar coordinates lie in compact polygons,
and their nonnegative t coordinates are bounded by the finite maximum
roof height (in fact at most 42), so the sets are compact.

At the point `(0,0,1/m,...,1/m)` all planar support inequalities are
strict, every t_j is positive, and the sum of the t coordinates is
1, strictly below each roof value 19,14,33/2. The point is therefore
interior in the FULL ambient R^d for each body. The halfspaces H_i
ignore t and pass through this common point. A small interior ball
is cut on both sides by every H_i, proving positive-volume proper
cuts without relying on projected areas.

The three cap normals form a minimal rank-two positive circuit in
R^d. Their closed halfspaces still cover the entire space. For d>2
this is not a full-rank normal family, and the source explicitly
states rank two; no rank-d conclusion should be inferred from the
planar introductory description.

## 2. Exact roof covariance and lifted homotheties

Write w=(11,1), so `phi_A(p)=19-w.p`. The planar cap maps have
ratios and translations

    lambda_1=3/4,   v_1=(0,-1/4),
    lambda_2=17/16, v_2=(-9/16,0),
    lambda_3=1,     v_3=(-1/2,1/2).

The three exact identities

    14-w.v_i=19 lambda_i

read `57/4=19(3/4)`, `323/16=19(17/16)`, and `19=19`.
Consequently, for every planar p, not just cap vertices,

    phi_B(lambda_i p+v_i)=lambda_i phi_A(p).

The midpoint identity follows as well, with
`rho_i=(1+lambda_i)/2`:

    phi_K(rho_i p+v_i/2)=rho_i phi_A(p).

The already verified planar cap maps are bijections between the
original endpoint caps. The roof identity preserves nonnegative
roof status in both directions, including zero-roof boundary points.
Together with `t -> lambda_i t`, it therefore gives an exact set
bijection between the lifted caps. It is a positive homothety of
the entire R^d, with translation `(v_i,0)`. The midpoint map is the
analogous homothety with ratio rho_i. Thus

    B^d intersect H_i=lambda_i(A^d intersect H_i)+(v_i,0),
    K^d intersect H_i=((A^d intersect H_i)+(B^d intersect H_i))/2.

Every map statement holds on all boundaries, not just almost
everywhere. Positive volumes established in Section 1 then give
the exact d-dimensional captured-side BM root equalities.

## 3. Full Minkowski midpoint is actual

For two lifted points, their planar midpoint belongs to K by the
verified planar Minkowski identity. Their t midpoint is coordinatewise
nonnegative, and its coordinate sum is bounded by the average of
the two endpoint roofs. Because their roof gradients agree and
their constants average to 33/2, this average is exactly the K
roof at the planar midpoint. Hence

    (A^d+B^d)/2 subset K^d.

Conversely, every point of K^d belongs to at least one H_i. The
corresponding exact cap identity puts it in `(A^d+B^d)/2`. This
proves the reverse inclusion and the full set equality. The use
of the cover is legitimate for boundary points and zero-roof
fibers as well.

## 4. The correct truncated projections and nonhomothety

Projection requires a nonnegative roof, since all t_j are
nonnegative. Conversely, any planar point with nonnegative roof
admits t=0. Thus the projections are precisely
`A intersect {phi_A>=0}`, and analogously for B and K.

The original right-top A vertex `(2,-1)` has roof -2, and the
corresponding B and K vertices have roofs -3/2 and -7/4. They
are genuinely absent from the projections. Exact clipping gives

    proj A^d:
      (-1,2), (-2,-1), (2,-3), (9/5,-4/5),
    proj B^d:
      (-13/8,17/8), (-5/2,-1/2), (3/2,-5/2), (27/20,-17/20),
    proj K^d:
      (-21/16,33/16), (-9/4,-3/4), (7/4,-11/4), (63/40,-33/40).

The last two vertices of each row lie on its zero-roof line. All
remaining vertices have nonnegative roof, and the displayed edges
give the complete intersection polygons. In particular the source's
two endpoint projections are exactly correct.

The bottom endpoint edge vectors are both `(4,-2)`, whereas their
next, zero-roof edge vectors are `(-1/5,11/5)` and
`(-3/20,33/20)`. The latter ratio is 3/4. These are uniquely
oriented nonzero edges, so no positive homothety of the two
projections can have both required ratios. A positive homothety
of the lifted bodies would project to one of their planar
projections. It is therefore impossible. Classical full-dimensional
BM equality characterization now implies strict whole-body BM.

## 5. Measure and embedding scope

All lifted bodies are full dimensional and have finite positive
d-volume. Placing A^d and B^d at integer bases -1 and 1 gives
their actual midpoint K^d at the only intervening integer base;
the convex hull has no additional integer bases. The lifted caps
remain actual ambient halfspaces parallel to that integer axis.

No numerical d-volume, normalized cap fraction, global criticality,
or no-heavy condition for the lifts is claimed in Section 6.
The planar area and no-heavy assertions elsewhere in the source
must not be silently transferred to these lifts. The source
explicitly avoids that transfer. The verified conclusion is the
failure of global homothety under the proper positive cap-cover
BM equalities in every d>=3, with a rank-two cap circuit.

The independent polygon verifier
`supporting computation verify_cap_gluing_counterexample_and_origin_depths.py` includes
the exact roof coefficient identities, the nonnegative-roof clips,
and their cap maps. The all-dimensional step follows from the
coordinatewise positive homotheties and affine roof identities
proved above, rather than numerical dimension checks.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
